subject: Discovery follow-up: Lincore POC scope & model shortlist
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Li <sofia.li@lincore.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@lincore.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call — POC scope & model shortlist

Hi Sofia / Carlos — thanks again for the time today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we put the POC charter in writing.

Recap (call highlights)
- Goal: validate a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant that reduces average handle time by 20% and increases first-contact resolution for account setup flows.
- Primary languages: EN, ES (Spanish support required for Mexico ops).
- Data: product FAQs + knowledge base (S3), and a masked subset of recent anonymized support transcripts (~5k rows) for eval.

Proposed POC plan (high level) — 3 weeks active evaluation following kickoff
1) Week 0 (prep): data share, redwood sends POC charter & test plan (attached).
2) Week 1: model onboarding + baseline runs on your sample set; initial tuning and prompt policy.
3) Week 2: evaluation window (5k queries, 10% Spanish); metric collection and qualitative review.
4) Week 3: wrap, ROI/ops review, go/no-go decision + handoff doc.

Success criteria (suggested, happy to modify)
- Accuracy / quality: intent-classification F1 >= 0.86 and top-1 answer correctness >= 82% (human-evaluated).
- Latency: median generation latency <= 400ms (95th <= 1200ms) for English; Spanish SLA target median <= 550ms.
- Hallucination: documented hallucination rate < 2% on sampled outputs.
- Cost: projected per-1k-query cost improvement >= 15% vs current baseline.

Model shortlist & fallback rationale
- Primary model (recommended): Llama 3 13B (4-bit quantized profile) — good balance of instruction-following and latency/cost for your conversational throughput.
- Fallback low-latency option: Mistral Instruct 8B (quantized) — used for low-latency routing on short transactional prompts and high-concurrency bursts.
- Multilingual support: we’ll include a Spanish prompt prefix + small targeted tuning set; both models have acceptable Spanish performance for chat-style tasks but we’ll measure per the eval plan.

Ownership & contacts
- Redwood sales lead / exec sponsor: Neha Kapoor (me) — scope, timelines, contract questions.
- Technical lead / onboarding: Rishi Malhotra — model config, benchmarks, infra.
- CS / success: Marcus Lin — acceptance criteria, ops handoff.

Attachments: POC-charter-v1.pdf (high-level plan), model-benchmarks.csv (sample perf data).

Next steps
- I’ll drop the POC charter & test-set checklist into the Drive and HubSpot right after this.
- Can you confirm: (1) a short Spanish test set (200 utterances) is available; (2) whether you need an on-prem/private deployment ask?
- Proposed kickoff: Dec 14 or Dec 15 — does either work for your team?

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachment stubs:
- POC-charter-v1.pdf (12 pages)
- model-benchmarks.csv (sample rows, 250 lines)

From: Sofia Li <sofia.li@lincore.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@lincore.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: Lincore POC scope & model shortlist

Hi Neha — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Yes, we can provide a 200-utterance Spanish validation set and we’ll package a masked transcript extract for the 5k window.
- Data residency: we need to confirm whether PII will touch Redwood-hosted endpoints during the eval. If we de-identify on our side it should be fine, but we need SOC2 evidence and to understand retention windows for logs. Please include the SOC2 report link and your default data retention policy in the charter.
- Usage estimate: we expect ~150k queries/month during the trial if this scales; would that change your recommended model or deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated)?

Model question: does the Llama 3 13B option support the latency SLAs you listed at our expected concurrency (~120 concurrent sessions)? If not, please propose the trade-offs.

Kickoff: Dec 14 is preferable for our schedule.

Thanks,
Sofia Li
Head of AI, Lincore
sofia.li@lincore.com | +52 55 1234 6789

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Li <sofia.li@lincore.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@lincore.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: Lincore POC scope & model shortlist

Sofia — quick technical notes to address your questions and to lock in the eval plan.

1) Residency / PII: if you de-identify before upload we treat all artifacts as non-PII for the POC. For SOC2 and compliance: attaching a link to our SOC2 summary in the charter; we can also share the auditor report under an NDA. Default retention: logs/trace data kept 30 days for POC; we can extend to 90 days upon request.

2) Model performance & concurrency tradeoffs
- Llama 3 13B (q4) should meet the latency median <=400ms at moderate concurrency if configured on dedicated throughput instances (batching + KV cache). At sustained 120 concurrent interactive sessions we recommend either: (A) Redwood Dedicated pool for predictable latency; or (B) host with autoscale + burst reservations but expect higher variance on p95.
- Fallback policy: route short transactional prompts (<= 40 tokens expected) to Mistral Instruct 8B quantized; route long context generative flows to Llama 3 13B. This keeps tail latency down during spikes.

3) Evaluation plan & metrics (concrete)
- Dataset: 5k queries (10% ES), split 80/20 for tuning vs held-out evaluation.
- Metrics: top-1 correctness (human label) target >=82%; intent F1 >=0.86; median latency targets as above; hallucination rate <2% on random sample of 500 outputs.
- AB plan: run 50/50 split for a 48-hour window comparing Redwood config vs current in-house baseline on production-like traffic replay. Collect both quantitative + 100 blind qualitative labels.

4) Benchmarks & config (attachments)
- model-benchmarks.csv: sample latency / token-cost rows from a similar customer baseline.
- routing-policy-stub.yaml: short policy showing byte/length-based routing and penalty for tail latency.

Operational asks
- Provide the masked transcript as S3 paths + an IAM role OR upload via the secure Drive link in the charter.
- Confirm whether you want us to test with prefix caching enabled (recommended for long-session reuse).

If you confirm the December 14 kickoff, I’ll reserve infra and start model pre-warm.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stubs:
- model-benchmarks.csv (attached sample)
- routing-policy-stub.yaml (policy example)

Thanks — all clear. We can de-identify on our side and will upload the masked transcripts to the Drive folder by Dec 10. SOC2 report: please send the auditor summary in the charter (NDA already signed).

Dec 14 kickoff works for us; please send a calendar invite with a short agenda (data handoff, infra plan, success metric alignment, milestones). Also confirm whether Redwood will need a temporary dedicated pool for the first 72 hours of the evaluation (we approve budget for that if recommended).

Looking forward to it.

Best,
Sofia
